threads.body: `appendOperationToSummary()` now calls `yytext()`, which allocates a new `String` for every operation token (SELECT/INSERT/...). This sanitizer runs on the hot path, so it’s worth avoiding the extra allocation by appending directly from the lexer buffer (similar to `appendCurrentFragment()`).

threads.body: [Testing] The EXPLAIN rule now appends the matched token text (case-preserving) via appendOperationToSummary(), but the current test coverage only exercises the uppercase form ("EXPLAIN SELECT ..."). Adding a mixed/lowercase EXPLAIN test would better lock in the new behavior and prevent regressions back to normalized/constant casing.

threads.body: This new parameterized test asserts query-summary behavior unconditionally by calling `ANALYZER.analyzeWithSummary(...)`, which makes it run (and potentially fail) even when `emitStableDatabaseSemconv()` is false. Most other tests in this class use the `analyze(...)` helper and/or `assumeTrue(emitStableDatabaseSemconv())` to keep the suite valid in both stability modes. Consider gating this test to stable semconv and using `analyze(...)` for consistency.
changing `FROM` to `from` isn't relevant, but it does match what's seen from hibernate, so seems more realistic example data

In the JPQL/HQL `FROM`-starts-a-query fallback, the summary currently always prefixes with the lowercase synthetic operation `select`. With `%ignorecase` enabled, queries that start with `FROM ...` (uppercase) will now produce a query summary starting with `select ...`, which does not preserve the original keyword casing/style. Consider deriving the synthetic SELECT casing from the matched `FROM` token’s first character so uppercase `FROM` yields `SELECT` while lowercase `from` yields `select`.
